react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge with overwhelming statistical confidence on a single biological story: the tryptophan metabolism pathway is the dominant affected system in this treatment-versus-control comparison. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 / Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (FDR=9.58×10⁻¹⁵, 6 of 54 pathway compounds observed, fold enrichment 667), with WP:WP465 and the Reactome module R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) following at ranks 2 and 3. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 as the sole significant hit (p=1.59×10⁻⁸, 6 of 41 compounds), and mummichog m/z-direct activity mapping scored Tryptophan metabolism as its top pathway (p=8.40×10⁻⁵, 13 of 14 compounds overlapping the empirical network). The six driver metabolites span the canonical trunk of this pathway: L-tryptophan (C00078, CHEBI:16828) as the entry substrate, its decarboxylation product tryptamine (C00398), the decarboxylated/oxidized indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), the downstream neurotransmitter serotonin (C00780), the acetylated melatonin (C01598), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), a kynurenine-branch intermediate. The simultaneous perturbation of the serotonin/melatonin arm and the kynurenine arm suggests the treatment disrupts tryptophan allocation between neuroactive and immunomodulatory branches. Doxycycline (C06973), acrolein (C01471), and milrinone (C07224) were detected as differential metabolites but do not map to the tryptophan network in any of the three tools, suggesting they may represent off-target treatment effects or co-administered agents. Note: the compound annotated as cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (C00127) resolves to glutathione disulfide in ChEBI, indicating an annotation error in the input list rather than a true pathway signal.
